newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan copper futures not needed--industry chief.
newsitem.headline: Japan copper futures not needed--industry chief.

text.p: The newly appointed chief of a leading Japanese non-ferrous metals industry group said on Monday he saw no need to list a copper futures contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM).
"I'm not really sure why they would do this," said Yumi Akimoto at his first news conference after his appointment as chairman of the Japan Mining Industry Association (JMIA).
Akimoto is also president of Mitsubishi Materials Corp, a leading Japanese copper smelting company.
He said a futures contract should be listed if people who actually use the metal saw a need for it.

He pointed out, however, that two other industry associations, the Japan Brass Makers Association and the Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers' Association, had also said they saw no need for a TOCOM copper futures contract.

Akimoto said the London Metal Exchange already offered a transparent market for determining world prices and expressed concern that speculators with no direct involvement in metals would wield influence over pricing if copper futures were listed on TOCOM.

TOCOM President Naozo Mabuchi said in January the exchange planned to launch futures contracts for copper, lead and zinc within four to five years. Aluminium futures are already scheduled to begin trading on TOCOM in April.
